name: HOTEL CHAM CHAM - Taipei
detail: Visited in Oct 2019. Hotel has the bare minimum (no pool, no gym) I need for my trip which mostly revolves travelling out to other areas in Taipei. + Toilet has a bidet + Both a shower and tub is present + TV channels were from a TV box and were more than adequate. + Hotel and rooms have a modern design + Attentive staff who replaced the shower and soap when we're almost done with it + Halloween decorations + blood (tomato) juice available at reception Conveniently located near Banqiao station which has 3 main lines - HSR, TRA and Taipei Metro. Makes it easy to get to airport via HSR (+1 transfer onto the Airport Line) and to Taipei Main Station. Located on the Blue Taipei Metro line, Ximen is just a few stops away. Breakfast is not an issue as there is a shop that sells cheap traditional Taiwanese breakfast right opposite the hotel. 2 Family Marts located beside the Hotel and a larger one located in Banqiao station which sells all the souvenir that you need (e.g. ChiaTe)

name: Caesar Park Hotel Banqiao
detail: Facilities were up to date, rooms were clean and spacious.

name: Solaria Nishitetsu Hotel Taipei Ximen
detail: Hotel very clean and staff always willing to help if needed.

name: Dolamanco Hotel
detail: Superb. The hotel is right beside bus and metro stations, restaurants and shops and in easy reach of monuments and places of interest. The hotel staff speak English and give good advice, help with bookings and information. Value for money without lacking quality. Good and plentiful food, breakfast only was served. Everything was as advertised. Plenty of bathroom products were available, replenished daily. Bottled water and snacks were also provided and re-stocked daily. There is no seating in the lobby, but you get what you pay for and they look after your luggage when you have checked out. I stayed an extra night as the Challin Hotel let me down by not providing access to their accomodation. I really enjoyed my stay at this convenient Taipei Hotel.

name: Taipei Fullerton Hotel - South
detail: Taipei hotels are expensive to begin with, so this is not an exception. Location is great, less than 100 metres away from Da-an MRT. Surrounded by eating places. Rooms are modern and very clean. Small but for a solo traveller or couple, can seem cozy. This hotel is geared primarily to the business traveller, but thankfully, not as formal and intimidating. The best thing is that you will not find bus loads of tourists here.

name: The Howard Plaza Hotel Taipei
detail: fairly good sized rooms, great location - 1 block from sogo (5 minute walk) like the larger hotel feel, more services/amenities requested early checkin and room was available upon very early arrival - big plus/bonus! service was efficient and friendly all around wifi in the rooms is a bit spotty/slow - as with many hotels in taipei bathrooms are dated, but not a huge deal for us

name: CityInn Hotel Taipei Station Branch III
detail: The hotel itself was perfectly fine, the room was fairly large (compared to most Taipei hotels) and there were a lot of amenities (e.g. free cup noodles at night, coffee machine, free laundry and toiletries). But what really sold me on this hotel was their attentiveness to guests. When arriving, the hotel manager (Henry) was very careful to explain nearby attractions. The next day, I received a thoughtful text message from him telling me that he had prepared a weather forecast and itinerary under my hotel room door (along with a cute af rabbit drawing). The itinerary was so detailed it planned restaurant locations for me! For laundry, my significant other had a few items to wash, and as the washing machines were full at the time, the lobby staff did the laundry for us. Even after leaving, the management messages to say goodbye and that if we need anything (ie ordering souvenirs) to let them know! All in all, will come back again and a must stay in Taipei! Best location!

name: Cityinn Hotel Plus Fuxing N.Rd. Branch
detail: We booked this hotel based on positive reviews on Tripadviser and were not disappointed. The hotel is very new, tastefully-decorated and is 2-minutes’ walk from subway station. The room is bright and modern, with nice bed and linens. Although the room is a bit small after opening two suitcases, we find it very comfortable. Bathroom is functional and shower has good pressure. The slight drawback is poor sound-proof. We initially stayed on 12/f, which is the second highest floor in the hotel. The next morning, we heard water running and people talking, so loud that we almost thought someone was in our room. We reported the issue to the staff and were quickly assigned a room on 13/f and had no problem since. We are very impressed with all the staff we dealt with and would like to mention two in particular. We emailed to ask where to fix an iphone screen in Taipei on the evening before we arrived at Taipei. Mr. Peter Kan replied in an hour, telling us there is no Apple Store in Taiwan yet but gave us an indicative price for fixing it elsewhere. We had no idea how Peter got this information late at night but was very happy to have received an answer so quickly. As the hotel provides service to purchase souvenirs for guests, my mum paid hotel staff Miss. Maruka (? Sorry we forgot her name but know she’s from Hualien and speaks Japanese) TWD1,000 to get pineapple pies. She left the hotel for sightseeing in a rush and forgot to take her change, which was around TWD600. Upon her return in the evening, before she even asked, staff handed her the exact change without missing a penny and a letter was sent to her room apologizing for the hotel staff’s oversight. She was very touched and impressed, as everything was done in cash without record, it would be easy for staff not to return the change but they didn’t. Instead, they showed complete professionalism and honesty, which leaves my mum and me a great impression. We would like to thank the hotel for an excel
